interview: What is Java and why is it popular?

Java is a general-purpose, object-oriented, strongly typed language that compiles to bytecode and runs on the JVM. It is popular for portability, a huge ecosystem (Spring, Hibernate, Kafka), automatic memory management, strong tooling and backward compatibility.
Is Java purely object-oriented?
No. Java has eight primitive types (int, double, boolean and so on) that are not objects, and static members that belong to no instance. Everything else lives inside classes.
Why is Java called platform independent?
javac compiles source to bytecode, which is the same on every OS. Each platform has its own JVM that translates bytecode to native instructions, so the program itself does not change.
Is Java compiled or interpreted?
Both. Source is compiled to bytecode by javac, then the JVM interprets that bytecode and JIT-compiles hot methods to machine code at run time.
What are the main differences between Java and C++?
Java has no pointers or manual memory management, no multiple inheritance of classes, no operator overloading, and runs on a VM. C++ compiles directly to native code and gives low-level control.
What does public static void main(String[] args) mean?
public: the JVM can call it from outside. static: no object is needed to call it. void: it returns nothing. main: the name the JVM looks for. String[] args: command-line arguments.

Machine code for the current CPU
javac is the compiler; its output is platform-neutral bytecode, which the JVM then runs.

What is JAVA_HOME and why is it needed?
It points to the JDK installation. Tools like Maven, Gradle, Tomcat and IDEs use it to find the right Java version.
Can one file contain more than one class?
Yes, but at most one can be public, and the file must be named after that public class.
How do you pass arguments to a Java program?

What does the PATH variable do?
It tells the OS where to find executables, so adding the JDK bin directory lets you run javac and java from any folder.

keypoints: No pointers, no operator overloading and no multiple class inheritance, which removes common sources of bugs.
Encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and abstraction are built into the language.
Bytecode runs on any JVM, so there is no re-compile per OS.
No raw pointers, bytecode verification and the security manager/sandbox model limit what code can do.
Strong typing, checked exceptions and garbage collection catch or prevent many errors.
Threads, executors and the java.util.concurrent package are part of the platform.
The JIT compiler turns hot bytecode into native machine code at run time.
Built-in networking (java.net, RMI) and classes that load on demand at run time.
interview: List the main features of Java.
Simple, object-oriented, platform independent, secure, robust, multithreaded, high performance (JIT), distributed and dynamic.
What does "write once, run anywhere" mean?
Source code is compiled once into bytecode, and that same bytecode runs unchanged on any operating system that has a JVM.
What are the Java buzzwords?

The traits Java was designed around: simple, object-oriented, portable, platform independent, secure, robust, architecture neutral, interpreted, high performance, multithreaded, distributed and dynamic.
Why does Java have no pointers?
Pointers allow direct memory access, which causes crashes and security holes. Java uses references managed by the JVM instead.
Which C++ features did Java leave out to stay simple?
Explicit pointers, pointer arithmetic, operator overloading for user classes, multiple inheritance of classes, header files and manual memory management.
How is Java secure?
No pointer arithmetic, bytecode verification before execution, class loader isolation and access control through the security architecture.
What does the bytecode verifier do?
It checks loaded bytecode for illegal operations, such as breaking access rights or using wrong types, before any of it runs.
What is the role of the class loader in security?
It loads classes on demand and keeps code from the local file system separate from code that arrived over the network.
Is the Security Manager still used?
It is deprecated for removal since Java 17. Modern applications rely on containers, OS permissions and module boundaries instead.
Why is Java called robust?
Strong compile-time type checking, exception handling, automatic garbage collection and no unsafe memory access.
How does garbage collection help, and can you force it?
It reclaims objects that are no longer reachable, so you do not free memory by hand. System.gc() is only a request; the JVM decides when to collect.
Why is Java called both compiled and interpreted?
javac compiles source to bytecode, then the JVM interprets that bytecode and the JIT compiler turns hot methods into native code.
What is the role of the JIT compiler?
It compiles frequently executed bytecode to native machine code while the program runs, so long-running programs become much faster than pure interpretation.
What is the difference between platform independent and architecture neutral?
Platform independent means the same bytecode runs on different operating systems. Architecture neutral means the language has no implementation-dependent features, for example int is always 4 bytes.
What is bytecode, and who produces and runs it?
Bytecode is the instruction set of the JVM. The compiler (javac) produces it in .class files and the JVM loads, verifies and executes it.
Why is Java not 100% object oriented?
Because of primitive data types and static members, which exist outside objects.
Does Java support multiple inheritance?
Not for classes, which avoids the diamond problem. A class can implement many interfaces, so multiple inheritance of type is supported.
How does Java support multithreading?
Through the Thread class and Runnable interface, the executor framework and the java.util.concurrent package. Threads share one memory area, so they use less memory than separate programs.
What does it mean that Java is distributed?
It has built-in networking (java.net, sockets, HTTP client) and tools such as RMI that let a program call methods on objects living on another machine.
What does it mean that Java is dynamic?
Classes are loaded on demand when first needed, new code can be linked at run time, and Java can call native C and C++ code through JNI.
Why is Java slower to start than C but fast once it is warmed up?
The JVM must start, load classes and interpret code first. After profiling, the JIT compiles hot code to native code, which can match or beat ahead-of-time compiled code.
How would you explain the features of Java to a beginner in one minute?

Java is easy to read, runs anywhere through bytecode and the JVM, protects memory with references and a verifier, recovers from errors with exceptions and garbage collection, and can do many tasks at once with threads.
mcq: Which feature removes direct memory access in Java?
Java uses references instead of pointers, so code cannot read or write arbitrary memory.
Bytecode is the same everywhere; the JVM adapts it to the machine.

The Just-In-Time compiler produces native code for frequently used methods.

Primitives such as int and boolean are not objects.

Modern apps rely on containers and OS permissions.
On-demand loading is part of what makes Java dynamic.

Source is compiled to bytecode, which the JVM interprets and JIT-compiles

try and catch let a program handle errors and continue.

keypoints: Java Virtual Machine: loads, verifies and executes bytecode; it is platform specific.

JDK contains JRE, and JRE contains JVM: JDK = JRE + dev tools, JRE = JVM + libraries.

interview: Explain the difference between JDK, JRE and JVM.
The JVM executes bytecode. The JRE is the JVM plus the standard libraries, enough to run a program. The JDK is the JRE plus development tools such as javac, so you can write and build programs.
Is the JVM platform independent?
No. The JVM is platform specific (there is one for each OS and CPU). Java is platform independent because the same bytecode runs on any of those JVMs.
What are the main components of the JVM?
The class loader subsystem, the runtime data areas (heap, stack, method area, PC registers, native method stack) and the execution engine with the interpreter, JIT compiler and garbage collector.
Do you need the JDK to run a Java program?
You only need a Java runtime to run a compiled program. You need the JDK to compile it.
What does the class loader do?
It loads .class files into memory on demand, links them (verify, prepare, resolve) and initialises them.
Where are objects stored in the JVM?
On the heap. Local variables and method calls live on the stack of each thread.

The JDK bundles javac and the other development tools.
JDK includes JRE, which includes JVM
JDK = JRE + tools; JRE = JVM + libraries.

Classes, interfaces, arrays and enums; the variable holds a reference to an object on the heap.

Local (inside a method), instance (one per object) and static (one per class).

interview: What are the primitive data types in Java?
byte, short, int, long, float, double, char and boolean.
What is the difference between primitive and reference types?
A primitive variable stores the value itself; a reference variable stores the address of an object on the heap. Primitives cannot be null and have no methods.
What is the default value of an uninitialised local variable?
There is none. Local variables must be assigned before use or the code does not compile. Fields get default values (0, false, null).
Why does float f = 3.14; not compile?
3.14 is a double literal; assigning it to a float would lose precision. Write 3.14f or cast it.
What happens when you cast a larger type to a smaller one?
Data can be lost or overflow. For example, (byte) 130 becomes -126 because only the lowest 8 bits are kept.
What is the difference between instance, static and local variables?
Instance variables belong to each object, static variables are shared by the class and exist once, and local variables exist only while a method runs.
mcq: How many primitive data types does Java have?
byte, short, int, long, float, double, char and boolean.
What is the size of an int in Java?
int is always 32 bits, on every platform.
Which declaration causes a compile error?
3.14 is a double and cannot be narrowed to float without a cast or the f suffix.
What is the default value of a boolean field?
Casting to int truncates the decimal part; it does not round.
Only reference types can be null; primitives cannot.

keypoints: private, default (package-private, no keyword), protected and public.
Visible only inside the same class.
Visible to classes in the same package; used when no modifier is written.
Same package, plus subclasses in other packages (through inheritance).
Can only be public or default; private and protected apply to members and nested classes.
Keep fields private and expose them through public getters and setters.
Start with the most restrictive modifier and widen only when needed.
interview: What are the access modifiers in Java and how do they differ?
private: same class only. default: same package. protected: same package and subclasses. public: everywhere.
What is the difference between default and protected?
Both allow access within the package. protected additionally lets subclasses in other packages use the member through inheritance.
Can a top-level class be private?
No. A top-level class can only be public or package-private. Private and protected are allowed for nested classes.
Why should fields normally be private?
It enforces encapsulation: the class controls how its data changes, can validate input and can change its internals without breaking callers.
Can a private method be overridden?
No. A private method is not visible to subclasses, so a method with the same signature in a subclass is a new method, not an override.
Can you reduce visibility when overriding?
No. An overriding method cannot be more restrictive than the method it overrides (public cannot become protected).
mcq: Which modifier allows access only within the same class?
What is the visibility when no modifier is written?
Which modifier lets a subclass in another package access a member?
protected extends package access to subclasses.
Which is a valid modifier for a top-level class?
Top-level classes are public or package-private.
Which order goes from most to least restrictive?
private is narrowest, public is widest.

keypoints: + - * / % ; int / int drops the decimals, so 7 / 2 is 3 and 7 % 2 is 1.
== != > < >= <= always give a boolean; use equals() (not ==) to compare String contents.
&& and || short-circuit: the right side is skipped when the left already decides the result.
& and | on booleans always evaluate both sides, which matters when the right side has side effects.
i++ uses the old value then adds 1; ++i adds 1 then uses the new value.
+=, -=, *= include an implicit cast: byte b = 10; b += 5; compiles, b = b + 5; does not.
condition ? a : b is an expression that returns a value, a compact if-else.
& | ^ ~ work on bits; << multiplies by 2 per shift, >> keeps the sign, >>> fills with zeros.
Unary > multiplicative > additive > shift > relational > equality > && > || > ternary > assignment; use brackets when unsure.
Checks the runtime type before a cast and avoids ClassCastException; Java 16+ supports pattern matching: if (o instanceof String s).
interview: What is the difference between = and ==?
= assigns a value. == compares: for primitives it compares values, for objects it compares references (are they the same object).
What does 7 / 2 give, and why?
3. Both operands are int, so integer division drops the decimal part. Use 7 / 2.0 or (double) 7 / 2 to get 3.5.
What is short-circuit evaluation?
With && the right side is evaluated only if the left is true; with || only if the left is false. It saves work and prevents errors such as obj != null && obj.isReady().
What is the difference between i++ and ++i?
Post-increment returns the old value then increments; pre-increment increments first and returns the new value. int i = 5; int a = i++; gives a = 5, i = 6. int b = ++i; gives b = 7.
Difference between && and &?
&& is logical and short-circuits. & on booleans evaluates both sides; on integers it is bitwise AND.
Does Java support operator overloading?
No. The only built-in overload is + for String concatenation. This keeps behaviour of operators predictable.
What is the difference between >> and >>>?
>> is the signed right shift: it copies the sign bit, so negative numbers stay negative. >>> is the unsigned right shift and fills with zeros.
Why does 10.0 / 0 not throw but 10 / 0 does?
Floating-point division follows IEEE 754 and returns Infinity (or NaN for 0.0/0). Integer division by zero has no valid result, so it throws ArithmeticException.
mcq: What is the value of 7 / 2 in Java when both are int?
Integer division truncates the decimal part.
What does int a = 5; int b = a++ + ++a; make b?
a++ gives 5 (a becomes 6), ++a makes a 7 and gives 7, so b = 5 + 7 = 12.
&& and || stop evaluating once the result is known; & and | do not.
The condition is true, so the first value is returned.
Which operator checks an object type at run time?
instanceof tests whether an object is an instance of a class or interface.
Shifting right by one divides by 2 for non-negative numbers.
Floating-point division by zero gives Infinity; only integer division throws.

Runs a block only when the condition is true.
Exactly one of the two blocks runs.
Conditions are checked top to bottom; the first true one wins and the rest are skipped.
The condition must be a boolean: if (x = 5) is a compile error in Java (unlike C).
Without { } only the next statement belongs to the if; always use braces to avoid bugs.

Runs when no case matches; it can appear anywhere, but is usually last.
Java 14+ switch expressions use -> and yield a value with no fall-through.
The inner condition is evaluated only when the outer one is true.
interview: What are control statements in Java?
Statements that control the order of execution: selection (if, if-else, switch), iteration (for, while, do-while) and jump (break, continue, return).
What is fall-through in switch?
If a case has no break, execution continues into the next case labels until a break or the end of the switch. It is sometimes used on purpose to group cases.
Can a switch use a String?
Yes, since Java 7. It uses equals() internally, so case values are compared by content and are case sensitive. null causes a NullPointerException.
Which types are allowed in switch?
byte, short, char, int (and their wrappers), String and enum. long, float, double and boolean are not allowed.
Is if (x = 5) valid in Java?
No. The condition must be boolean and x = 5 is an int, so it does not compile. if (flag = true) compiles but is almost always a bug.
What is the difference between if-else-if and switch?
if-else-if can test any boolean condition and ranges. switch compares one value to constants and is cleaner for many fixed choices.
What is a switch expression?
A Java 14+ form: String s = switch (day) { case 1, 7 -> "Weekend"; default -> "Weekday"; }; It returns a value, has no fall-through and must be exhaustive.
mcq: Which statement is NOT a decision-making statement?
What happens if break is missing in a switch case?
Execution falls through to the next case
Without break, the following cases also execute until a break is found.
Which type is NOT allowed in a switch expression selector?
long, float, double and boolean cannot be used in switch.
What is the output? int x = 5; if (x > 3) System.out.print("A"); else System.out.print("B");
5 > 3 is true, so the if branch runs.
if requires a boolean; x = 5 is an int assignment.
In an if-else-if ladder, how many blocks run?
The first true condition runs and the rest are skipped.
Which is the modern arrow form of switch called?
Switch expressions (Java 14+) use -> and return a value.

keypoints: Immediately exits the nearest loop or switch.
Skips the rest of the current iteration and moves to the next one.
Exits the current method, optionally giving back a value.
break outer; exits the loop labelled outer, useful to leave nested loops at once.
continue outer; jumps to the next iteration of the labelled outer loop.

The update must happen before continue, otherwise the loop can repeat forever.
A statement placed right after break, continue or return is a compile error.
interview: What is the difference between break and continue?
break ends the whole loop (or switch). continue ends only the current iteration and goes on with the next one.
What is a labelled break?
A break that names an outer loop: outer: for (...) { for (...) { if (x) break outer; } } leaves both loops at once.
Can break be used outside a loop or switch?
No, it causes a compile error. A labelled break may be used on a labelled block.
What does return do in a void method?
return; ends the method immediately without a value.
What happens to the for-loop update after continue?
It still runs. continue jumps to the update expression, then the condition is checked again.
Does code after a break statement run?
No, and the compiler rejects statements directly after it as unreachable.
mcq: continue moves straight to the next iteration.

The loop stops when i is 3, before printing it.
What is printed? for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { if (i == 3) continue; System.out.print(i); }
Only the iteration for 3 is skipped.
How do you leave two nested loops at once?
A labelled break exits the labelled outer loop.

keypoints: Best when the number of iterations is known: for (init; condition; update).
Checks the condition first; may run zero times.
Runs the body once before checking the condition, so it always runs at least once.

for (;;) and while (true) run until a break or return.

A variable declared in the for header exists only inside the loop.

list.forEach(x -> ...) (Java 8) is the functional alternative for collections.
interview: What is the difference between while and do-while?
while tests first and may not run at all. do-while runs the body first, then tests, so it executes at least once.
When would you use for instead of while?
When the number of iterations is known up front (counter based). while suits loops that depend on a condition that changes inside the body.
What is an enhanced for loop and its limitations?
It iterates over arrays and Iterables without an index. You cannot know the index, iterate backwards, or remove elements from a collection while looping (that throws ConcurrentModificationException).
How do you create an infinite loop and stop it?
while (true) { ... } or for (;;) { ... }; stop with break, return, or by throwing an exception.
What is the output of for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++); System.out.print(i)?
It does not compile: the stray semicolon makes the loop body empty and i is out of scope after the loop.
How many times does a nested loop run for i < 3 and j < 4?
12 times (3 * 4) for the inner body.
mcq: Which loop always runs at least once?
do-while checks its condition after the body.
How many times does for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) run?
Which loop is best for iterating over every element of an array?
for (int x : arr) reads each element without an index.
Runs forever until break or return
What is printed? int i = 10; do { System.out.print(i); i++; } while (i < 5);
The body runs once before the condition is checked.
How many iterations occur for two nested loops of 3 and 4?
The inner loop runs fully for each outer iteration: 3 * 4.

interview: What is a package and why do we use it?
A namespace that groups related types. It prevents name conflicts, organises code, and works with access modifiers (default and protected are package based).
Is import java.util.*; importing sub-packages too?
No. It imports only classes directly in java.util, not java.util.concurrent or others.
Which package is imported automatically?
java.lang.
What if two packages contain a class with the same name?
Import one and use the fully qualified name for the other, for example java.sql.Date.
Does the package statement have to be first?
Yes. Only comments and blank lines may appear before it, and there can be only one per file.
What is the difference between import and static import?
import makes classes usable by simple name; static import makes static members (methods and constants) usable without the class name.
mcq: package must be the first statement of the file.
Which package is imported by default?
Does import java.util.*; include java.util.concurrent classes?
Wildcard imports do not include sub-packages.
The package com.shop.model maps to which folder path?

Where must the package statement appear?
It must come before everything except comments.

How do you print an array?
Arrays.toString(a) for 1D and Arrays.deepToString(a) for multi-dimensional arrays. Printing a directly shows a type and hash code.
What is the difference between an array and an ArrayList?
An array has a fixed size and can hold primitives. ArrayList grows dynamically, holds objects only and offers many methods.
What is a jagged array?
A 2D array whose rows have different lengths, created by allocating each row separately.
Can an array be empty?
Yes, new int[0] is valid and has length 0. A null array reference is different and throws NullPointerException when used.

interview: How do you find the largest element in an array?
Keep a variable max starting at a[0]; loop through the array and update max when a[i] > max. Time O(n), space O(1).
How do you reverse an array in place?
Use two indexes, i = 0 and j = n - 1, and swap while i < j. No extra array is needed.
How do you find the second largest element?
Track largest and secondLargest in one pass: update both when a value exceeds largest, and update secondLargest when it is between the two.
How do you check whether an array is sorted?
Loop from 1 to n - 1 and return false if a[i] < a[i - 1]. An empty or single element array is sorted.
How do you remove duplicates?
Insert elements into a LinkedHashSet and convert back; or sort the array and copy only elements different from the previous one.
How do you merge two sorted arrays?
Use two pointers and always copy the smaller current element to the result; copy leftovers at the end. O(n + m).

interview: Why is String immutable in Java?
For security (class names, URLs, passwords), thread safety, caching of hashCode and the string pool, which saves memory by sharing literals.
What is the difference between == and equals() for Strings?
== checks whether both references point to the same object; equals() checks whether the characters are the same. "a" == "a" is true because of the pool, but new String("a") == "a" is false.
String vs StringBuilder vs StringBuffer?
String is immutable; StringBuilder is mutable and fast but not thread safe; StringBuffer is mutable and synchronised.
How many objects does String s = new String("hi"); create?
Up to two: the literal "hi" in the pool (if not already there) and a new object on the heap.
Why is concatenating in a loop slow?
Each + creates a new String, copying all characters, which makes the loop O(n squared). Use StringBuilder.append.
How do you compare two strings ignoring case?
equalsIgnoreCase(other) or compareToIgnoreCase(other).

interview: What is a constructor and how is it different from a method?
A constructor initialises a new object, has the class name, no return type and is called by new. A method has a return type, is called on an object and describes behaviour.
When does the compiler provide a default constructor?
Only when the class has no constructors. If you write any constructor, the default one is not added.
Can a constructor be private?
Yes. It is used in singleton classes and factory-method patterns to stop outside code from creating objects.
Can we call a constructor explicitly?
Only from another constructor with this(...) or super(...), as the first statement.
Can a constructor be overridden?
No. Constructors are not inherited, so there is nothing to override. They can be overloaded.
What is the output order for a child object?
The parent constructor runs first, then the child constructor, because super() is called implicitly.

interview: What is constructor chaining?
Calling one constructor from another, either in the same class with this(...) or in the parent with super(...), so initialisation code is written once.
Why must this() or super() be the first statement?
The object must be partly initialised by the parent or the other constructor before this constructor uses it.
Can you use this() and super() in the same constructor?
No. Each must be first, so only one is allowed. If you use this(), the other constructor eventually calls super().
What happens if two constructors call each other?
Compile error: recursive constructor invocation.
What is the order of execution for Child extends Parent?
Parent constructor body first, then Child body, since Child calls super() as its first action.

interview: What does static mean in Java?
The member belongs to the class itself, not to any instance. It is loaded once and shared by all objects.
Why is main declared static?
The JVM starts the program without creating an object of the class, so main must be callable on the class.
Can a static method access instance variables?
Not directly, because no object exists. It needs an object reference: obj.name.
Can static methods be overridden?
No. A subclass can declare a static method with the same signature, but that hides the parent method (method hiding).
When does a static block run?
Once, when the class is first loaded and initialised, before any constructor or static method call.
Difference between static and instance variables?
A static variable has one shared copy per class; an instance variable has a separate copy in each object.

A final variable cannot be reassigned; a final method cannot be overridden; a final class cannot be subclassed.
If a reference is final, can the object change?
Yes. final fixes the reference only. A final List can still have items added.
What is a blank final variable?
A final field declared without a value; it must be assigned exactly once, in the constructor or an initialiser block.
Difference between final, finally and finalize?
final is a keyword for constants and restrictions; finally is the block that always runs after try; finalize() is a deprecated method called by the GC before reclaiming an object.
Why is String final?
To keep it immutable and safe: nobody can subclass it and change its behaviour.

interview: What are wrapper classes and why are they needed?
Object versions of primitives. They are needed for collections and generics, to hold null, and to use utility methods such as parsing.
What are autoboxing and unboxing?
Automatic conversion between a primitive and its wrapper: Integer a = 10 (boxing) and int b = a (unboxing).
Why does Integer a = 127, b = 127; a == b give true but 128 gives false?
Integer caches objects for -128 to 127, so both references point to the same object. Outside that range new objects are created; use equals().

NullPointerException, because the compiler calls intValue() on null.
Difference between parseInt and valueOf?
parseInt returns a primitive int; valueOf returns an Integer object.
